title: Capacity burst egress plan and tenant preemption matrix
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: During peak traffic patterns customers using Dedicated capacity have observed transient bursts that exhaust reserved pools. Our current soft-spillover to hosted runs into cost spikes, unpredictable latency, and customer complaints. We need a tempered egress strategy that balances availability with predictable unit economics and clear tenant preemption rules.

Goals:
- Define deterministic rules for when a request is routed from Dedicated -> Hosted as a controlled egress (not blind spillover).
- Provide a tenant preemption matrix and eviction priority that protects high-SLA customers while allowing best-effort workloads to be throttled or delayed.
- Ensure region-awareness (avoid cross-region egress unless explicitly allowed by tenant policy).
- Expose controls and telemetry in Console for ops and customers (preflight simulation, estimated cost delta, and TTL for egressed sessions).

Scope:
- Routing decision logic in orchestrator and gateway layer (policy + preflight).
- Per-tenant config surface (soft cap, hard cap, preemption tier, cross-region allowance).
- Graceful eviction of KV cache pinned sessions and KV rehydration hints to Hosted model variants.
- Console UI for egress simulation and per-route cost estimates.

Out of scope for this ticket: implementing quantization or new kernels; those are tracked separately.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Routing policy implemented: orchestrator rejects blind spillover and applies egress decision only after preflight check; 2) Tenant preemption matrix defined and stored in tenant config; 3) Eviction order implemented (least-recently-used best-effort tenants -> best-effort model variants -> hub-hosted fallback) with documented rollback; 4) Console shows egress simulation for a tenant, including estimated per-token cost delta and latency delta; 5) Tests: unit tests for policy evaluation, integration test simulating capacity exhaustion, and a canary run in staging with synthetic tenants.
technical_notes:
Policy flow proposed:
- Step 1 (Capacity check): Check dedicated pool availability and active queue length + predicted tail latency (95p) for the route.
- Step 2 (Preflight cost check): If dedicated is saturated, compute cost and latency delta of routing to hosted based on model variant mapping and region egress settings.
- Step 3 (Preemption decision): Consult tenant preemption tier: Tier A (SLA-critical) -> no egress unless emergency override; Tier B (business-critical) -> allow egress up to soft cap; Tier C (best-effort) -> allow egress and subject to throttling.
- Step 4 (Eviction order): If we must free memory or GPUs: a) abort queued best-effort requests, b) flush unpinned KV caches for Tier C, c) reassign GPU slots according to token-weighted fairness.

Numbers for implementation (initial):
- Soft cap default: 80% of tenant reserved RPS; hard cap: 110% with egress only for Tier B/C and cost-shift tag.
- Circuit breaker: if hosted egress error rate > 3% for 5m, disable egress for the region for 10m.
- Prefetch eviction grace: 30s rehydration hint TTL for KV cache entries evicted due to preemption.

Model variant mapping: prefer smaller quantized variants for hosted egress (e.g., v1-int8 instead of v1-fp16) unless tenant forces parity variant. Add a variant fallback order in tenant config.
decision_log:
2026-03-03 - Design review: agreed to make egress a declared action (tagged on billing) rather than implicit spillover.
2026-03-05 - Ops feedback: require per-tenant simulation before enabling auto-egress in production. Added egress-simulation API.
2026-03-09 - Security review (preliminary): cross-region egress must be opt-in at tenant level; KMS keys must follow destination region policy.
